answer: One defense is a sponsorship grove with a hard horizon: each established agent may sponsor only a few newcomers, and the sponsorship fee doubles with every child, like a jade carving that gets pricier with each cut. A newcomer must also survive a public probation window, during which a gale of independent checks can flag fake behavior. If any descendant is caught, the sponsor loses all fees and its own standing, so running a thousand sockpuppets means paying an exponential bill and risking the whole grove at once.
